D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Read/write: vendor describes MCP as read-only; all 12 documented tools retrieve/search data or skill instructions. No annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are published. 2. Confirmation: no server-enforced confirmation mechanism documented. Tool text asks agents to ask for user inputs in some workflows; not an approval gate for data writes. 3. Permissions: OAuth metadata identifies authorization server and grants, but no scopes_supported; docs describe Daloopa login, API-key token (24 hours), and X-API-KEY. User-role inheritance, revocation, allowlists, OAuth lifetime, and redirect approval not found. Expert transcripts require firm feature enablement. 4. Modes: no read-only switch, tool filters, query-free mode, or regional MCP endpoint documented. Product is described as read-only; expert calls are feature-gated. 5. Data protection: Daloopa privacy disclosure says access logs cover authentication events, accessed tickers, and usage frequency; prompts/queries and LLM outputs are not systematically collected/stored. It claims encrypted transit and restricted/audited internal access. 6. Limits: document search prompt says 1–10 keywords, up to 10 matching documents, and 120 requests/minute/API key; get_document_content caps returned content at MCP_SECTION_MAX_CHARACTERS without publishing its value. Other limits not found. 7. Validation/correction: prompts specify date formats, required inputs and workflow rules; server-side rejection, coercion, or operator overrides are not documented. 8. Monitoring: privacy disclosure says access logs and internal analytics; no opt-out or MCP action audit detail documented. 9. Vendor-interest: no feedback/rating/survey/report tool in the official tool list; no MCP upsell messages identified. 10. Behaviour: official tool descriptions include proactive-call, citation, formatting, period-selection, and ask-before-fetching instructions; external Claude/Codex plugins distribute 21 skills but are not tools in the hosted server list. 11. Memory/state: no agent-history-dependent behavior documented; firm feature enablement affects transcript availability. 12. Structure: one flat tool list documented for financial endpoint; docs search MCP is a separate endpoint. 13. Escape hatches: no raw API, SQL, script, or arbitrary request tool listed.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: Official list exists at https://docs.daloopa.com/docs/daloopa-mcp: it names 10 tools, despite an introductory sentence saying “Three tools.” The official Tool Prompts page documents 12 tool definitions; the two additional names are discover_comparable_companies_metrics and get_comparable_companies_fundamentals. actions.json contains all 12 official names and adds no catalogue-only tools. Tedix and Manufact each report 3 tools; Obot describes capabilities but supplies no list in the collected page; Claude connector directory has no detailed tool list in the collected page. These catalogue counts conflict with the official documentation’s 10-name reference and 12 prompt definitions.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public code for the deployed server or verbatim initialize/tool definitions established as the hosted endpoint's complete payload. The tool prompt page provides developer-facing prompt examples, not confirmed hosted tool definitions; no estimate substituted.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The official API-versus-MCP page lists API capabilities beyond MCP, including company model status, bulk company subscriptions, and usage/consumption endpoints. These REST API operations are not among the 12 documented MCP tools. Source: https://docs.daloopa.com/docs/api-vs-mcp

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The tool prompts advise citation formats, search triggers, metric selection, period formatting, financial table orientation, and user input collection. For example: “DO NOT wait for the user to explicitly request a document search.” The documentation does not establish that these are server-enforced constraints.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The MCP privacy disclosure says: “MCP access is strictly read-only. Third parties cannot write to, upload to, or modify any Daloopa data via the protocol.” It says Daloopa does not systematically collect/store user prompts or queries, nor LLM outputs; access logs include authentication events, accessed tickers, and usage frequency. It also claims encrypted transit, restricted and monitored internal access, and no sale/sharing of collected MCP user data or logs.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The vendor says every output derived from a Daloopa datapoint maps to a source, and product materials describe data points as hyperlinked to original source documents. The MCP product page calls the service a read-only remote server secured with OAuth.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Read-only promise is consistent with the documented tool purposes: all 12 are retrieval, search, discovery, or skill-instruction tools. No public server code or tool annotations were found to independently verify enforcement. Citation and formatting requirements appear as text instructions, not verified enforcement. Privacy and logging statements are policy disclosures rather than observable MCP behavior.

contradictions: Input endpoint /mcp returns OAuth-protected 401, and its provided protected-resource metadata declares resource https://mcp.daloopa.com/server/mcp; official docs identify /server/mcp as the financial MCP URL. No tool manifest specific to input path /mcp was found, so documented endpoint tools are used as best available evidence and this endpoint-path discrepancy remains unresolved.
Official introduction says “Three tools” but its Available Tools list names 10; official Tool Prompts documents 12 definitions, including two taxonomy tools absent from the Available Tools list.

Third-party Tedix and Manufact listings report 3 tools, matching discover_companies, discover_company_series, and get_company_fundamentals only; this is fewer than the official reference list and Tool Prompts list. These catalogues are not used to replace the official names.
observations_for_research: The published prompt instructions include proactive tool selection and output-format directives, while public evidence does not show whether the hosted implementation enforces them.
The reference page's introductory count, its own list, and the more extensive Tool Prompts page show different tool totals; this can affect an agent's perceived available capabilities.

Daloopa distributes a 21-skill workflow library separately from the MCP tool list; documentation describes MCP tools for discovering and fetching skill instructions, while the skill implementations are external plugin files.
